# Shell: reference

The prompt, navigation, history search, aliases, colors and the help card that Gash adds to an interactive Bash. The guide is [README.md](README.md); this page lists every function, alias and command, as their own help prints it (`gash_help NAME`, `gash COMMAND --help`).

## Functions

| Function | Alias | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`all_colors`](#all_colors) |  | Display all 256 terminal colors |
| [`gash_inspiring_quote`](#gash_inspiring_quote) |  | Display a random quote, optionally with its source |
| [`hgrep`](#hgrep) |  | Smart history search with timestamps and deduplication |
| [`history_grep`](#history_grep) | `hg` | Search command history with colored output |
| [`mkdir_cd`](#mkdir_cd) | `mkcd` | Create a directory and cd into it |
| [`path_add`](#path_add) |  | Add directories to PATH once each |

### all_colors

Display all 256 terminal colors.

#### Usage

```text
all_colors
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Test your terminal's color support
all_colors
```

#### Notes

```text
Colors only on a color terminal: piped, or with NO_COLOR set, it prints
the color names alone.
```

### gash_inspiring_quote

Display a random quote, optionally with its source.

#### Usage

```text
gash_inspiring_quote [--source]
```

#### Examples

```bash
# The quote shown under the banner
gash_inspiring_quote

# Where it was said or written
gash_inspiring_quote --source
```

#### Notes

```text
Quotes live in quotes/list.txt: one `"Text." — Author` line each,
under a `# ` line with the source (book, essay, talk, mail; a link
where one exists). New quotes need a source that can be checked;
see CONTRIBUTING.md.
```

### hgrep

Smart history search with timestamps and deduplication.

#### Usage

```text
hgrep PATTERN [OPTIONS]
```

#### Options

```text
-n, --limit N       Show only the N most recent matches (0: all)
-a, --all           Include hgrep/history_grep commands in results
-r, --reverse       Newest first (default: oldest first)
-j, --json          Output as JSON array
-H, --no-highlight  Disable highlighting / force plain output
-E, --regex         PATTERN is a Go regular expression (RE2 syntax),
                    case-insensitive; an invalid regex is an error
-c, --count         Only show the count of unique matching commands
-g, --group         Collapse similar commands under a shared chain prefix
    --pick          Fuzzy-select a matching command via fzf and print it
    --no-color      Disable colored output for this invocation
-h, --help          Show this help (anywhere before --)
--                  End of options: the next word is PATTERN
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Search for git push commands
hgrep "git push"

# Last 10 docker commands
hgrep docker -n 10

# Export history as JSON
hgrep deploy -j

# Count how many times you ran a command
hgrep "npm install" -c

# Regex: git push or pull at the start
hgrep -E "^git (push|pull)"

# Group "cd X && ..." variants under one prefix
hgrep cd -g

# Fuzzy-pick a past git command (needs fzf)
hgrep git --pick

# Newest first
hgrep kubectl -r

# A pattern that starts with "-"
hgrep -- --force
```

#### Notes

```text
Matching is case-insensitive; PATTERN is a fixed string unless -E.
Commands are deduplicated (the last run wins) and listed oldest first.
-n N keeps the N most recent matches, with or without -r.
```

#### Output format

```text
[2024-01-15 14:52:01] git push origin main
[2024-01-15 15:10:22] git commit -m "fix"

With --json:
[{"timestamp":"2024-01-15 14:52:01","epoch":1705330321,"count":1,"command":"git push origin main"},...]
```

See also: [`history_grep`](../shell/reference.md#history_grep)

### history_grep

Search command history with colored output.

Alias: `hg`

#### Usage

```text
history_grep PATTERN...
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Find all git commands in history
hg git

# Find docker-compose commands
hg "docker compose"

# Find SSH connections
hg "ssh "
```

#### Notes

```text
Simple and fast. For advanced features (timestamps,
deduplication, JSON output), use hgrep instead.
The words are joined with spaces into one pattern (a GNU grep basic
regex, case-insensitive) matched against each command. Column 2 is a
command's first two words, column 3 the rest; duplicates and the
history_grep/hg lines themselves are left out.
```

See also: [`hgrep`](../shell/reference.md#hgrep)

### mkdir_cd

Create a directory and cd into it.

Alias: `mkcd`

#### Usage

```text
mkdir_cd DIRECTORY
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Create and enter a new project directory
mkcd my-new-project

# Create nested directories and enter
mkcd ~/projects/client/frontend
```

#### Notes

```text
Exactly one DIRECTORY, taken as a name: -p creates ./-p and - creates
./-. CDPATH is not searched, and nothing is printed.
```

### path_add

Add directories to PATH once each.

#### Usage

```text
path_add [--append] DIR...
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Toolchains first, in this order, only those that exist
path_add ~/.local/bin ~/.cargo/bin ~/.config/composer/vendor/bin

# At the end of PATH instead
path_add --append /opt/tools/bin
```

#### Notes

```text
Directories that do not exist are skipped and one already in PATH stays
where it is, so running it again (or re-sourcing ~/.gashrc) never makes
PATH grow. GASH_PATH_ADD in ~/.gash_env does this for every new shell.
```

## Aliases

Defined in interactive shells, in packs. The Defined column says when an alias exists; empty means always.

### The colors pack

`grep` gets `--color=auto` when the system's grep supports it.

| Alias | Runs | Defined |
|---|---|---|
| `grep` | `grep --color=auto` |  |

### The navigation pack

`ls`, `ll`, `la`, `l`, `lash`, `sl`, `dir` and `vdir` also get the color option of the system's `ls` (`--color=auto` on GNU, `-G` on BSD and macOS) when it has one.

| Alias | Runs | Defined |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | `ls` |  |
| `ll` | `ls -l` |  |
| `la` | `ls -la` |  |
| `l` | `ls -CF` |  |
| `lash` | `ls -lash` |  |
| `sl` | `ls` |  |
| `dir` | `dir` |  |
| `vdir` | `vdir` |  |
| `..` | `cd ..` |  |
| `...` | `cd ../..` |  |
| `cd..` | `cd ..` |  |
| `....` | `cd ../../..` |  |
| `.....` | `cd ../../../..` |  |
| `.4` | `cd ../../../..` |  |
| `.5` | `cd ../../../../..` |  |
| `cls` | `clear` |  |
| `path` | `tr ":" "\n" <<<"$PATH"` |  |

### The safety pack

Interactive and verbose forms of the commands that overwrite or delete. On by default: `GASH_SAFETY_ALIASES=0` in `~/.gash_env` turns off those of `cp`, `mv`, `mkdir`, `rm`, `chown`, `chmod` and `chgrp` (see [configuration](../configuration.md)); `bc`, `ports`, `reboot` and `shutdown` stay. The `--preserve-root` forms need GNU coreutils.

| Alias | Runs | Defined |
|---|---|---|
| `cp` | `cp -iv` |  |
| `mv` | `mv -iv` |  |
| `mkdir` | `mkdir -pv` |  |
| `rm` | `rm -Iv --one-file-system --preserve-root` |  |
| `chown` | `chown --preserve-root` |  |
| `chmod` | `chmod --preserve-root` |  |
| `chgrp` | `chgrp --preserve-root` |  |
| `bc` | `bc -l` |  |
| `ports` | `ss -tulanp` |  |
| `reboot` | `sudo /sbin/reboot` |  |
| `shutdown` | `sudo /sbin/shutdown` |  |

### The general pack

With `GASH_REPLACE_TOOLS=1`, Gash also aliases standard commands to their richer replacements when those are installed: see [configuration](../configuration.md).

| Alias | Runs | Defined |
|---|---|---|
| `quit` | `services_stop` |  |
| `less` | `most` | with GASH_REPLACE_TOOLS=1, when most is installed |
